text:
Maya: Quick callout  the console wants to let PMs apply a saved query to a route as a canary. Need API shape for bindings + a lightweight cost preview. Opinions?

Theo: +1 to bindings as their own resource (/bindings). Keeps lifecycle (draft, canary, active). Binding fields: id, saved_view_id, scope (route:id), pinned_model, active_version, staged_overrides, rollout_state.

Ravi: For cost preview let's call billing/estimate with route_id + view_snapshot (filters + pinned_model) and qps hint. Sync call ok for modal open if estimator is fast; otherwise stub and refresh. Return tokens_per_hour and cost_delta_cents.

Sofia: UX: modal should show tiny diff vs current route filters, tokens/day estimate, and a canary slider (1%,5%,25%). Also 'Apply as draft' option so users can save without rolling out.

Theo: Telemetry: fire console.event = "binding.preview" and "binding.apply". preview payload includes tokens_estimate and preview_sample_rate. apply includes rollout_id, ramp_percent, binding_id.

Ravi: Implementation note: staged_overrides should be opaque JSON blob on binding so we don't have to model every filter change server-side. Keep base_view_version to diff.

Maya: Back-compat: create bindings for existing saved_views with scope=global at migration time; clients unchanged unless they use bindings API.

infra-bot: deploy: ui-bindings-modal v1.0.0-canary deployed to prod-us-1 :rocket:

Sofia: I'll prototype the modal and include the cost chip next to Apply. Will post Figma link.

Theo: I'll open a small API PR with schema + example payloads and a migration plan.

Ravi: I'll add estimator endpoint docs and a quick perf SLA. If estimator >200ms we fallback to async.

Maya: Great. Target: ship canary next week after PR+estimator are in. Thanks folks.
